claim: The Endosomal Sorting Complexes Required for Transport (ESCRT) machinery mediates the membrane fission step that completes cytokinetic abscission and separates dividing cells.
source: The Endosomal Sorting Complexes Required for Transport (ESCRT) machinery mediates the membrane fission step that completes cytokinetic abscission and separates dividing cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work establishing ESCRT's role in abscission.

claim: ESCRT-III filaments constrict membranes of the intercellular bridge midbody to the abscission point.
source: Filaments composed of ESCRT-III subunits constrict membranes of the intercellular bridge midbody to the abscission point.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to previous studies on ESCRT-III filament function.

claim: ESCRT-III filaments bind and recruit cofactors whose activities help execute abscission and/or delay abscission timing in response to mitotic errors via the NoCut/Abscission checkpoint.
source: These filaments also bind and recruit cofactors whose activities help execute abscission and/or delay abscission timing in response to mitotic errors via the NoCut/Abscission checkpoint.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research on ESCRT-III cofactors and checkpoint regulation.

claim: The ESCRT-III subunit IST1 binds the cysteine protease Calpain-7 (CAPN7).
source: We previously showed that the ESCRT-III subunit IST1 binds the cysteine protease Calpain-7 (CAPN7) and that CAPN7 is required for both efficient abscission and NoCut checkpoint maintenance (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Wenzel et al., 2022).

claim: CAPN7 is required for both efficient abscission and NoCut checkpoint maintenance.
source: We previously showed that the ESCRT-III subunit IST1 binds the cysteine protease Calpain-7 (CAPN7) and that CAPN7 is required for both efficient abscission and NoCut checkpoint maintenance (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Wenzel et al., 2022).

claim: The tandem microtubule-interacting and trafficking (MIT) domains of CAPN7 bind simultaneously to two distinct IST1 MIT interaction motifs.
source: Here, we report biochemical and crystallographic studies showing that the tandem microtubule-interacting and trafficking (MIT) domains of CAPN7 bind simultaneously to two distinct IST1 MIT interaction motifs.
evidence: This claim is supported by biochemical and crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Structure-guided point mutations in either CAPN7 MIT domain disrupted IST1 binding in vitro and in cells.
source: Structure-guided point mutations in either CAPN7 MIT domain disrupted IST1 binding in vitro and in cells, and depletion/rescue experiments showed that the CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for (1) CAPN7 recruitment to midbodies, (2) efficient abscission, and (3) NoCut checkpoint arrest.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from binding assays and cellular experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for CAPN7 recruitment to midbodies.
source: Structure-guided point mutations in either CAPN7 MIT domain disrupted IST1 binding in vitro and in cells, and depletion/rescue experiments showed that the CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for (1) CAPN7 recruitment to midbodies, (2) efficient abscission, and (3) NoCut checkpoint arrest.
evidence: This claim is supported by depletion/rescue experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for efficient abscission.
source: Structure-guided point mutations in either CAPN7 MIT domain disrupted IST1 binding in vitro and in cells, and depletion/rescue experiments showed that the CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for (1) CAPN7 recruitment to midbodies, (2) efficient abscission, and (3) NoCut checkpoint arrest.
evidence: This claim is supported by depletion/rescue experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: The CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for NoCut checkpoint arrest.
source: Structure-guided point mutations in either CAPN7 MIT domain disrupted IST1 binding in vitro and in cells, and depletion/rescue experiments showed that the CAPN7-IST1 interaction is required for (1) CAPN7 recruitment to midbodies, (2) efficient abscission, and (3) NoCut checkpoint arrest.
evidence: This claim is supported by depletion/rescue experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: CAPN7 proteolytic activity is required for abscission and checkpoint maintenance.
source: CAPN7 proteolytic activity is also required for abscission and checkpoint maintenance.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using catalytically inactive CAPN7 mutants presented in the manuscript.

claim: IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies, where its proteolytic activity is required to regulate and complete abscission.
source: Hence, IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies, where its proteolytic activity is required to regulate and complete abscission.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Humans express 12 distinct ESCRT-III proteins that are recruited to membrane fission sites throughout the cell, including to midbodies that connect dividing cells during cytokinesis.
source: Humans express 12 distinct ESCRT-III proteins that are recruited to membrane fission sites throughout the cell, including to midbodies that connect dividing cells during cytokinesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge of the ESCRT-III protein family.

claim: Within the midbody, ESCRT-III proteins copolymerize into filaments that constrict the membrane to the fission point.
source: Within the midbody, ESCRT-III proteins copolymerize into filaments that constrict the membrane to the fission point (Guizetti et al., 2011; Elia et al., 2011; Mierzwa et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2020; Pfitzner et al., 2021; Azad et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: ESCRT-III filaments recruit VPS4 AAA+ ATPases, which dynamically remodel the filaments to drive midbody constriction.
source: ESCRT-III filaments also recruit a variety of cofactors, including the VPS4 AAA+ ATPases, which dynamically remodel the filaments to drive midbody constriction (Elia et al., 2012; Mierzwa et al., 2017; Pfitzner et al., 2020; Pfitzner et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Many ESCRT-III cofactors contain microtubule-interacting and trafficking (MIT) domains, which bind differentially to MIT-interacting motifs (MIMs) located near the C termini of the different human ESCRT-III proteins.
source: Many of these cofactors contain microtubule-interacting and trafficking (MIT) domains, which bind differentially to MIT-interacting motifs (MIMs) located near the C termini of the different human ESCRT-III proteins (Hurley and Yang, 2008; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A quantitative survey of the human ESCRT-III-MIT interactome revealed a series of novel interactions between ESCRT-III subunits and MIT cofactors.
source: Our recent quantitative survey of the human ESCRT-III-MIT interactome revealed a series of novel interactions between ESCRT-III subunits and MIT cofactors, and implicated a subset of these cofactors in abscission and NoCut checkpoint maintenance (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Wenzel et al., 2022).

claim: CAPN7 is a ubiquitously expressed but poorly understood cysteine protease that had not previously been linked to abscission or to the NoCut checkpoint.
source: One such cofactor was Calpain-7 (CAPN7), a ubiquitously expressed but poorly understood cysteine protease that had not previously been linked to abscission or to the NoCut checkpoint.
evidence: This claim is based on the state of knowledge prior to the authors' previous work.

claim: CAPN7 contains tandem MIT domains that can bind specifically to the ESCRT-III subunit IST1.
source: CAPN7 contains tandem MIT domains that can bind specifically to the ESCRT-III subunit IST1 (Osako et al., 2010; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The CAPN7-IST1 interaction can activate CAPN7 autolysis and proteolytic activity towards non-physiological substrates.
source: This interaction can activate CAPN7 autolysis and proteolytic activity towards non-physiological substrates (Osako et al., 2010; Maemoto et al., 2013), although authentic CAPN7 substrates are not yet known.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Authentic CAPN7 substrates are not yet known.
source: This interaction can activate CAPN7 autolysis and proteolytic activity towards non-physiological substrates (Osako et al., 2010; Maemoto et al., 2013), although authentic CAPN7 substrates are not yet known.
evidence: This claim reflects the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The tandem CAPN7 MIT domains (CAPN7(MIT)2) bind a C-terminal region of IST1 that contains two distinct MIM elements.
source: The tandem CAPN7 MIT domains (CAPN7(MIT)2) bind a C-terminal region of IST1 that contains two distinct MIM elements (Figure 1A; Agromayor et al., 2009; Bajorek et al., 2009; Osako et al., 2010; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The double MIM IST1316-366 construct bound CAPN7(MIT)2 tightly with KD = 0.09 ± 0.01 µM.
source: The double MIM IST1316-366 construct bound CAPN7(MIT)2 tightly (KD = 0.09 ± 0.01 µM), with the C-terminal IST1 MIM element (IST1344-366) contributing most of the binding energy (KD = 1.8 ± 0.1 µM).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization anisotropy binding assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The C-terminal IST1 MIM element (IST1344-366) contributes most of the binding energy with KD = 1.8 ± 0.1 µM.
source: The double MIM IST1316-366 construct bound CAPN7(MIT)2 tightly (KD = 0.09 ± 0.01 µM), with the C-terminal IST1 MIM element (IST1344-366) contributing most of the binding energy (KD = 1.8 ± 0.1 µM).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence polarization anisotropy binding assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The N-terminal IST1 MIM element (MIM316-343) bound too weakly to measure accurately by FPA with KD > 100 µM.
source: The N-terminal IST1 MIM element (MIM316-343) bound too weakly to measure accurately by FPA (KD > 100 µM), so NMR titration experiments were performed to confirm the specificity and quantify the binding energy (KD = 200 ± 20 µM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by FPA and NMR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NMR titration experiments confirmed the specificity of the N-terminal IST1 MIM element binding and quantified the binding energy as KD = 200 ± 20 µM.
source: The N-terminal IST1 MIM element (MIM316-343) bound too weakly to measure accurately by FPA (KD > 100 µM), so NMR titration experiments were performed to confirm the specificity and quantify the binding energy (KD = 200 ± 20 µM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both IST1 MIM elements contribute to binding CAPN7(MIT)2.
source: These experiments demonstrated that both IST1 MIM elements contribute to binding CAPN7(MIT)2, in good agreement with previous measurements (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by binding assay data and citation to previous work.

claim: 20/55 IST1303-366 amide resonances displayed large (>15-fold) changes in peak intensity upon saturation binding of CAPN7(MIT)2.
source: 20/55 IST1303-366 amide resonances displayed large (>15-fold) changes in peak intensity upon saturation binding of CAPN7(MIT)2.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Residues with large peak intensity changes upon CAPN7(MIT)2 binding mapped exclusively to the two known IST1 MIMs.
source: These residues mapped exclusively to the two known IST1 MIMs (Figure 1D), again implicating both elements in CAPN7(MIT)2 binding and implying that residues outside of these elements do not contribute to binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR data and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Residues outside of the IST1 MIM elements do not contribute to CAPN7(MIT)2 binding.
source: These residues mapped exclusively to the two known IST1 MIMs (Figure 1D), again implicating both elements in CAPN7(MIT)2 binding and implying that residues outside of these elements do not contribute to binding.
evidence: This claim is inferred from NMR data showing that only MIM residues show significant binding-dependent changes.

claim: A minimal IST1 construct (IST1322-366, KD = 0.13 ± 0.01 µM) bound with the same affinity as the original construct (IST1316-366, KD = 0.11 ± 0.01 µM).
source: Consistent with this idea, a minimal IST1 construct (IST1322-366, KD = 0.13 ± 0.01 µM) bound with the same affinity as the original construct (IST1316-366, KD = 0.11 ± 0.01 µM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by FPA binding data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The crystal structure of the CAPN7(MIT)2–IST1322-366 complex revealed that each MIT domain binds a different MIM element.
source: The structure revealed that each MIT domain binds a different MIM element, which is a configuration that has not been documented previously (Figure 2A and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The configuration where each MIT domain binds a different MIM element has not been documented previously.
source: The structure revealed that each MIT domain binds a different MIM element, which is a configuration that has not been documented previously (Figure 2A and Table 1).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with existing structural literature.

claim: Both CAPN7 MIT domains form the characteristic three-helix MIT bundle structure.
source: Both CAPN7 MIT domains form the characteristic three-helix MIT bundle structure (Scott et al., 2005), and they are connected by a disordered six-residue linker.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and citation to prior structural work.

claim: The CAPN7 MIT domains are connected by a disordered six-residue linker.
source: Both CAPN7 MIT domains form the characteristic three-helix MIT bundle structure (Scott et al., 2005), and they are connected by a disordered six-residue linker.
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data.

claim: The N-terminal IST1 MIM element binds in an extended conformation in the helix 1/3 groove of the N-terminal CAPN7 MIT domain, making a canonical 'type 2' (MIM2) interaction.
source: The N-terminal IST1 MIM element binds in an extended conformation in the helix 1/3 groove of the N-terminal CAPN7 MIT domain, making a canonical 'type 2' (MIM2) interaction (Figure 2A, top, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Kieffer et al., 2008; Samson et al., 2008; Vild and Xu, 2014; Kojima et al., 2016; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and citations to prior structural work.

claim: The binding interface spans IST1 residues 324–332 (324VLPELPSVP332), which resembles the previously defined MIM2 consensus sequence (ΦPXΦPXXPΦP).
source: The binding interface spans IST1 residues 324–332 (324VLPELPSVP332), which resembles the previously defined MIM2 consensus sequence (ΦPXΦPXXPΦP, where Φ represents a hydrophobic residue and X a variable (often polar) residue; Kojima et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and citation to prior work defining the MIM2 consensus.

claim: The overall structure of the CAPN7-IST1 N-terminal MIM complex closely resembles the type 2 ESCRT-III-MIT complex formed by CHMP6168-179 bound to the VPS4A MIT domain.
source: Consistent with this observation, the overall structure closely resembles the type 2 ESCRT-III-MIT complex formed by CHMP6168-179 bound to the VPS4A MIT domain (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2; Kieffer et al., 2008; Skalicky et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison and citations to prior work.

claim: Sequence divergence at either end of the MIM core explains why the MIM2 element of CHMP6 binds preferentially to the VPS4A MIT domain, whereas the MIM2 element of IST1 prefers the first MIT domain of CAPN7.
source: Sequence divergence at either end of the MIM core appears to explain why the MIM2 element of CHMP6 binds preferentially to the VPS4A MIT domain, whereas the MIM2 element of IST1 prefers the first MIT domain of CAPN7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis and comparison.

claim: The C-terminal IST1 MIM element (349DIDFDDLSRRFEELKK364) forms an amphipathic helix that packs between helices 1 and 3 of the C-terminal CAPN7 MIT domain, making a canonical 'type 3' (MIM3) interaction.
source: The C-terminal IST1 MIM element (349DIDFDDLSRRFEELKK364) forms an amphipathic helix that packs between helices 1 and 3 of the C-terminal CAPN7 MIT domain, making a canonical 'type 3' (MIM3) interaction (Figure 2A, bottom, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Yang et al., 2008; Skalicky et al., 2012; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and citations to prior structural work.

claim: Core residues from the hydrophobic face of the IST1 helix are buried in the CAPN7 MIT helix 1/3 groove, and the interface hydrophobic contacts, hydrogen bonds, and salt bridges are nearly identical to those seen when this same IST1 motif makes a type 3 interaction with the MIT domain of SPARTIN.
source: Core residues from the hydrophobic face of the IST1 helix are buried in the CAPN7 MIT helix 1/3 groove, and the interface hydrophobic contacts, hydrogen bonds, and salt bridges are nearly identical to those seen when this same IST1 motif makes a type 3 interaction with the MIT domain of SPARTIN (Figure 2C; Guo and Xu, 2015; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by crystallographic data and citations to prior structural work.

claim: Thr95 of CAPN7 can be phosphorylated.
source: A previous study has reported that Thr95 of CAPN7 can be phosphorylated (Mayya et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Thr95 phosphorylation would reduce IST1 binding and could negatively regulate the CAPN7-IST1 interaction.
source: We therefore anticipate that Thr95 phosphorylation would reduce IST1 binding and could negatively regulate the CAPN7-IST1 interaction.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the structural position of Thr95 near the IST1 binding site.

claim: The selectivity of each CAPN7 MIT domain for its cognate IST1 MIM element binding is dictated by the character of the MIT binding grooves.
source: The selectivity of each CAPN7 MIT domain for its cognate IST1 MIM element binding is dictated by the character of the MIT binding grooves.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the binding interfaces.

claim: The hydrophobic contacts and hydrogen bonding potential of the residues within the N-terminal MIT domain are selective for type 2 interactions (IST1324-332), whereas the C-terminal MIT domain selects for type 3 interactions.
source: The hydrophobic contacts and hydrogen bonding potential of the residues within the N-terminal MIT domain are selective for type 2 interactions (IST1324-332), whereas the C-terminal MIT domain selects for type 3 interactions.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis and binding data.

claim: The CAPN7(MIT)2-IST1322-366 structure provides the first example of IST1325-336 bound to an MIT domain and confirms the expectation that this IST1 element engages in MIM2-type interactions.
source: In summary, the CAPN7(MIT)2-IST1322-366 structure (1) provides the first example of IST1325-336 bound to an MIT domain and confirms the expectation that this IST1 element engages in MIM2-type interactions, (2) demonstrates that IST1352-363 engages in a MIM3-type interaction when it binds CAPN7, and (3) shows that the separate IST1 MIM elements each bind distinct MIT domains within CAPN7(MIT)2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The structure demonstrates that IST1352-363 engages in a MIM3-type interaction when it binds CAPN7.
source: In summary, the CAPN7(MIT)2-IST1322-366 structure (1) provides the first example of IST1325-336 bound to an MIT domain and confirms the expectation that this IST1 element engages in MIM2-type interactions, (2) demonstrates that IST1352-363 engages in a MIM3-type interaction when it binds CAPN7, and (3) shows that the separate IST1 MIM elements each bind distinct MIT domains within CAPN7(MIT)2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The structure shows that the separate IST1 MIM elements each bind distinct MIT domains within CAPN7(MIT)2.
source: In summary, the CAPN7(MIT)2-IST1322-366 structure (1) provides the first example of IST1325-336 bound to an MIT domain and confirms the expectation that this IST1 element engages in MIM2-type interactions, (2) demonstrates that IST1352-363 engages in a MIM3-type interaction when it binds CAPN7, and (3) shows that the separate IST1 MIM elements each bind distinct MIT domains within CAPN7(MIT)2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The crystal structure of the CAPN7(MIT)2–IST1322-366 complex explains why IST1 binding is disrupted by the V18D mutation in the first CAPN7 MIT domain and by the F98D mutation in the second MIT domain.
source: The crystal structure of the CAPN7(MIT)2–IST1322-366 complex explains why IST1 binding is disrupted by the V18D mutation in the first CAPN7 MIT domain (magenta, Figure 2A, top) and by the F98D mutation in the second MIT domain (red, Figure 2A, bottom), as replacing either of these hydrophobic residues with charged residues would create unfavorable interactions in the hydrophobic cores of the MIT binding interfaces.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the mutation sites.

claim: Replacing V18 or F98 with charged residues would create unfavorable interactions in the hydrophobic cores of the MIT binding interfaces.
source: The crystal structure of the CAPN7(MIT)2–IST1322-366 complex explains why IST1 binding is disrupted by the V18D mutation in the first CAPN7 MIT domain (magenta, Figure 2A, top) and by the F98D mutation in the second MIT domain (red, Figure 2A, bottom), as replacing either of these hydrophobic residues with charged residues would create unfavorable interactions in the hydrophobic cores of the MIT binding interfaces.
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis and knowledge of protein chemistry.

claim: The control helix 1/2 mutation L61D was not expected to alter IST1 binding.
source: We also used the structure to design a control helix 1/2 mutation that was not expected to alter IST1 binding (L61D, cyan, Figure 2A, top).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis showing L61D is not in the binding interface.

claim: The single V18D or F98D mutations in CAPN7(MIT)2 each reduced IST1316-366 binding >20-fold, with a greater effect seen for the N-terminal MIT mutation (V18D).
source: Fluorescence polarization anisotropy binding assays showed that the single V18D or F98D mutations in CAPN7(MIT)2 each reduced IST1316-366 binding >20-fold, with a greater effect seen for the N-terminal MIT mutation (V18D) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by FPA binding assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The V18D/F98D double mutation decreased IST1316-366 binding even further (>300-fold vs. wt CAPN7(MIT)2).
source: The V18D/F98D double mutation decreased IST1316-366 binding even further (>300-fold vs. wt CAPN7(MIT)2).
evidence: This claim is supported by FPA binding assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The control L61D mutation did not affect IST1316-366 binding.
source: As predicted, the control L61D mutation did not affect IST1316-366 binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by FPA binding assay data presented in the manuscript.

claim: None of the CAPN7(MIT)2 mutations significantly disrupted the overall protein fold as assessed by circular dichroism spectroscopy.
source: Importantly, none of these mutations significantly disrupted the overall CAPN7(MIT)2 protein fold as assessed by circular dichroism spectroscopy (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by circular dichroism spectroscopy data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Full-length IST1 and CAPN7 proteins both eluted as monomers in SEC-MALS analyses.
source: SEC with multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS) analyses showed that the individual IST1 and CAPN7 proteins both eluted as monomers (IST1: calculated MW = 40.0 kDa, SEC-MALS estimated MW = 41 ± 1 kDa; CAPN7 calculated MW = 92.6 kDa, SEC-MALS estimated MW = 90.4 ± 0.3 kDa, see Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by SEC-MALS data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IST1 eluted anomalously rapidly from SEC, apparently because it adopts an extended conformation.
source: However, IST1 eluted anomalously rapidly, apparently because it adopts an extended conformation.
evidence: This claim is based on SEC data and inference about protein conformation.

claim: When mixed, full-length IST1 and CAPN7 formed a 1:1 complex that migrated even more rapidly than IST1 alone.
source: When mixed, full-length IST1 and CAPN7 formed a 1:1 complex that migrated even more rapidly.
evidence: This claim is supported by SEC data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Complex formation between full-length IST1 and CAPN7 was inhibited by inactivating mutations in the center of the two IST1 MIM elements interaction interfaces (L328D/L355A).
source: Importantly, complex formation was inhibited by inactivating mutations in the center of the two IST1 MIM elements interaction interfaces (L328D/L355A, see Figure 2A and Figure 3—figure supplement 3; Obita et al., 2007; Stuchell-Brereton et al., 2007; Kieffer et al., 2008; Bajorek et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by SEC data and citations to prior work on these mutations.

claim: The crystallographically defined MIT-MIM interactions mediate association of the full-length IST1 and CAPN7 proteins in solution.
source: Thus, the crystallographically defined MIT-MIM interactions also mediate association of the full-length IST1 and CAPN7 proteins in solution.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from SEC and mutagenesis data.

claim: Wild-type CAPN7 and the control CAPN7(L61D) mutant both co-precipitated IST1190-366 efficiently.
source: Wild-type CAPN7 and the control CAPN7(L61D) mutant both co-precipitated IST1190-366 and IST1 efficiently, whereas all three inactivating CAPN7 MIT point mutations (V18D, F98D, and V18D/F98D) dramatically reduced the co-precipitation of Myc-IST190-366 (no detectable binding) or Myc-IST1 (very low-level residual binding, indicating either non-specific background or minor contributions from other region(s) of the protein).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: All three inactivating CAPN7 MIT point mutations (V18D, F98D, and V18D/F98D) dramatically reduced the co-precipitation of Myc-IST190-366.
source: Wild-type CAPN7 and the control CAPN7(L61D) mutant both co-precipitated IST1190-366 and IST1 efficiently, whereas all three inactivating CAPN7 MIT point mutations (V18D, F98D, and V18D/F98D) dramatically reduced the co-precipitation of Myc-IST190-366 (no detectable binding) or Myc-IST1 (very low-level residual binding, indicating either non-specific background or minor contributions from other region(s) of the protein).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both crystallographically defined MIT:MIM binding interfaces mediate association of full-length CAPN7 and IST1 in vitro and in cell extracts.
source: Thus, both crystallographically defined MIT:MIM binding interfaces mediate association of full-length CAPN7 and IST1 in vitro and in cell extracts.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from multiple binding assays and co-IP experiments.

claim: IST1 localized in a double-ring pattern on either side of the central Flemming body within the midbody.
source: As expected, IST1 localized in a double-ring pattern on either side of the central Flemming body within the midbody (Agromayor et al., 2009; Bajorek et al., 2009), and wild-type CAPN7-mCherry colocalized with IST1 in the same pattern (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data and citations to prior work.

claim: Wild-type CAPN7-mCherry colocalized with IST1 in the same double-ring pattern at midbodies.
source: As expected, IST1 localized in a double-ring pattern on either side of the central Flemming body within the midbody (Agromayor et al., 2009; Bajorek et al., 2009), and wild-type CAPN7-mCherry colocalized with IST1 in the same pattern (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data and citation to prior work.

claim: CAPN7(C290S)-mCherry colocalized with endogenous IST1 on either side of the Flemming body.
source: CAPN7(C290S)-mCherry similarly colocalized with endogenous IST1 on either side of the Flemming body, whereas the two IST1 binding mutants did not (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The two IST1 binding mutants (V18D and F98D) did not colocalize with IST1 at midbodies.
source: CAPN7(C290S)-mCherry similarly colocalized with endogenous IST1 on either side of the Flemming body, whereas the two IST1 binding mutants did not (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Wild-type CAPN7 and CAPN7(C290S) colocalized with IST1 in ~80% of all IST1-positive midbodies.
source: Quantification revealed that wild-type CAPN7 and CAPN7(C290S) colocalized with IST1 in ~80% of all IST1-positive midbodies, whereas the two IST1 non-binding mutants colocalized with IST1 in <5% of midbodies (Figure 4B; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The two IST1 non-binding mutants colocalized with IST1 in <5% of midbodies.
source: Quantification revealed that wild-type CAPN7 and CAPN7(C290S) colocalized with IST1 in ~80% of all IST1-positive midbodies, whereas the two IST1 non-binding mutants colocalized with IST1 in <5% of midbodies (Figure 4B; Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies.
source: We conclude that IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies, and efficient localization requires that both CAPN7 MIT domains bind both IST1 MIM elements, whereas CAPN7 proteolytic activity is not required for proper localization.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from localization experiments with CAPN7 mutants.

claim: Efficient CAPN7 localization to midbodies requires that both CAPN7 MIT domains bind both IST1 MIM elements.
source: We conclude that IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies, and efficient localization requires that both CAPN7 MIT domains bind both IST1 MIM elements, whereas CAPN7 proteolytic activity is not required for proper localization.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from localization experiments with CAPN7 mutants.

claim: CAPN7 proteolytic activity is not required for proper localization to midbodies.
source: We conclude that IST1 recruits CAPN7 to midbodies, and efficient localization requires that both CAPN7 MIT domains bind both IST1 MIM elements, whereas CAPN7 proteolytic activity is not required for proper localization.
evidence: This claim is supported by localization data showing CAPN7(C290S) localizes normally.

claim: Depletion of CAPN7 from asynchronous HeLa cells increased the fraction of cells that stalled or failed at abscission.
source: As expected, depletion of CAPN7 from asynchronous HeLa cells increased the fraction of cells that stalled or failed at abscission, as reflected by significant increases in midbody stage cells (from 5 to 10%) and multinucleate cells, indicating failed abscission (from 6 to 22%) vs. control treatments (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CAPN7 depletion increased midbody stage cells from 5 to 10%.
source: As expected, depletion of CAPN7 from asynchronous HeLa cells increased the fraction of cells that stalled or failed at abscission, as reflected by significant increases in midbody stage cells (from 5 to 10%) and multinucleate cells, indicating failed abscission (from 6 to 22%) vs. control treatments (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CAPN7 depletion increased multinucleate cells from 6 to 22%.
source: As expected, depletion of CAPN7 from asynchronous HeLa cells increased the fraction of cells that stalled or failed at abscission, as reflected by significant increases in midbody stage cells (from 5 to 10%) and multinucleate cells, indicating failed abscission (from 6 to 22%) vs. control treatments (Figure 5A and B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Efficient abscission was almost completely rescued by expression of wild-type CAPN7-mCherry.
source: Efficient abscission was almost completely rescued by expression of wild-type CAPN7-mCherry, whereas abscission defects were not rescued by CAPN7 constructs that were deficient in IST1-binding (V18D or F98D) or proteolysis (C290S).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Abscission defects were not rescued by CAPN7 constructs that were deficient in IST1-binding (V18D or F98D) or proteolysis (C290S).
source: Efficient abscission was almost completely rescued by expression of wild-type CAPN7-mCherry, whereas abscission defects were not rescued by CAPN7 constructs that were deficient in IST1-binding (V18D or F98D) or proteolysis (C290S).

claim: Both IST1-binding and proteolytic activity are required for CAPN7 to support efficient abscission.
source: Thus, both IST1-binding and proteolytic activity are required for CAPN7 to support efficient abscission.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from rescue experiments with CAPN7 mutants.

claim: Nup153 depletion delays abscission and raises the proportion of midbody-stage cells to 23%.
source: In these experiments, NoCut signaling was maintained by Nup153 depletion, which delays abscission and raises the proportion of midbody-stage cells to 23% (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B; Mackay et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior work.

claim: Co-depletion of CAPN7 with Nup153 reduced the percentage of cells stalled at the midbody stage to 10%.
source: Co-depletion of CAPN7 reduced the percentage of cells stalled at the midbody stage to 10%, indicating that CAPN7 is required to maintain the NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by Nup153 knockdown, in good agreement with our previous study (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CAPN7 is required to maintain the NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by Nup153 knockdown.
source: Co-depletion of CAPN7 reduced the percentage of cells stalled at the midbody stage to 10%, indicating that CAPN7 is required to maintain the NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by Nup153 knockdown, in good agreement with our previous study (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior work.

claim: Rescue with wild-type CAPN7-mCherry restored NoCut checkpoint function almost completely (20% midbodies).
source: Rescue with wild-type CAPN7-mCherry restored NoCut checkpoint function almost completely (20% midbodies), whereas the IST1-binding or catalytically dead mutant CAPN7 constructs failed to rescue the checkpoint (all ~10% midbodies).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The IST1-binding or catalytically dead mutant CAPN7 constructs failed to rescue the NoCut checkpoint.
source: Rescue with wild-type CAPN7-mCherry restored NoCut checkpoint function almost completely (20% midbodies), whereas the IST1-binding or catalytically dead mutant CAPN7 constructs failed to rescue the checkpoint (all ~10% midbodies).
evidence: This claim is supported by rescue experiment data presented in the manuscript.

claim: CAPN7 must bind IST1 and be an active protease to participate in NoCut checkpoint regulation.
source: Hence, CAPN7 must bind IST1 and be an active protease to participate in NoCut checkpoint regulation.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from rescue experiments with CAPN7 mutants.

claim: CAPN7 and SPAST are required to sustain NoCut signaling when the checkpoint is triggered by co-depletion of nuclear pore proteins Nup153 and Nup50.
source: CAPN7 and the AAA ATPase Spastin (SPAST) are required to sustain NoCut signaling when the checkpoint is triggered by co-depletion of nuclear pore proteins Nup153 and Nup50 (Wenzel et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Treatment of asynchronous control HeLa cells with a low dose of ICRF-193 (80 nM) induced NoCut signaling, as reflected by increases in the proportion of cells with midbodies (from 5 to 11%) and multiple nuclei (from 4 to 8%).
source: Treatment of asynchronous control HeLa cells with a low dose of ICRF-193 (80 nM) induced NoCut signaling, as reflected by increases in the proportion of cells with midbodies (from 5 to 11%) and multiple nuclei (from 4 to 8%) (Figure 6A), in good agreement with previous reports (Bhowmick et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior work.

claim: Cells depleted of either SPAST or CAPN7 did not exhibit NoCut checkpoint responses following ICRF-193 treatments.
source: In these cases, however, ICRF-193 treatments did not induce further abscission defects/delays, implying that NoCut was not active in the absence of these proteins and therefore that SPAST and CAPN7 are required to sustain NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by DNA bridges.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: SPAST and CAPN7 are required to sustain NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by DNA bridges.
source: In these cases, however, ICRF-193 treatments did not induce further abscission defects/delays, implying that NoCut was not active in the absence of these proteins and therefore that SPAST and CAPN7 are required to sustain NoCut checkpoint signaling induced by DNA bridges.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with ICRF-193 treatment.

claim: Cells depleted of SPAST or CAPN7 did not exhibit NoCut checkpoint responses following aphidicolin treatments.
source: Specifically, control treatments of asynchronous HeLa cells with low doses of aphidicolin (0.4 µM) maintained checkpoint activation in both the presence and absence of KATNA1. In contrast, cells depleted of SPAST or CAPN7 did not exhibit NoCut checkpoint responses following aphidicolin treatments, indicating that both proteins are required to sustain NoCut signaling when the checkpoint is triggered by replication stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both SPAST and CAPN7 are required to sustain NoCut signaling when the checkpoint is triggered by replication stress.
source: Specifically, control treatments of asynchronous HeLa cells with low doses of aphidicolin (0.4 µM) maintained checkpoint activation in both the presence and absence of KATNA1. In contrast, cells depleted of SPAST or CAPN7 did not exhibit NoCut checkpoint responses following aphidicolin treatments, indicating that both proteins are required to sustain NoCut signaling when the checkpoint is triggered by replication stress.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with aphidicolin treatment.

claim: Proteolysis is critical for CAPN7 functions in NoCut and abscission.
source: Our data imply that proteolysis is critical for CAPN7 functions in NoCut and abscission, although physiological substrates have not yet been identified.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from experiments with catalytically inactive CAPN7.

claim: Physiological substrates of CAPN7 have not yet been identified.
source: Our data imply that proteolysis is critical for CAPN7 functions in NoCut and abscission, although physiological substrates have not yet been identified.
evidence: This claim reflects the current state of knowledge.

claim: GFP-CAPN7 can perform autolysis, and this activity is enhanced by IST1 binding.
source: GFP-CAPN7 can perform autolysis, and this activity is enhanced by IST1 binding (Osako et al., 2010), implying that interactions with IST1 could activate CAPN7 proteolytic activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Interactions with IST1 could activate CAPN7 proteolytic activity.
source: GFP-CAPN7 can perform autolysis, and this activity is enhanced by IST1 binding (Osako et al., 2010), implying that interactions with IST1 could activate CAPN7 proteolytic activity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from prior research showing IST1 enhances CAPN7 autolysis.

claim: CAPN7 has been proposed to function in ESCRT-dependent degradation of EGFR through the endosomal/MVB pathway.
source: In addition to our studies implicating CAPN7 midbody functions during cytokinesis, other biological functions for CAPN7 have also been proposed, including in ESCRT-dependent degradation of EGFR through the endosomal/MVB pathway (Yorikawa et al., 2008; Maemoto et al., 2014), and in human endometrial stromal cell migration and invasion (Liu et al., 2013) and decidualization (Kang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: CAPN7 has been proposed to function in human endometrial stromal cell migration and invasion.
source: In addition to our studies implicating CAPN7 midbody functions during cytokinesis, other biological functions for CAPN7 have also been proposed, including in ESCRT-dependent degradation of EGFR through the endosomal/MVB pathway (Yorikawa et al., 2008; Maemoto et al., 2014), and in human endometrial stromal cell migration and invasion (Liu et al., 2013) and decidualization (Kang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: CAPN7 has been proposed to function in decidualization.
source: In addition to our studies implicating CAPN7 midbody functions during cytokinesis, other biological functions for CAPN7 have also been proposed, including in ESCRT-dependent degradation of EGFR through the endosomal/MVB pathway (Yorikawa et al., 2008; Maemoto et al., 2014), and in human endometrial stromal cell migration and invasion (Liu et al., 2013) and decidualization (Kang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Aberrant CAPN7 expression may impair embryo implantation through a currently unknown mechanism.
source: Aberrant CAPN7 expression may also impair embryo implantation through a currently unknown mechanism (Yan et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: CAPN7 has evolutionarily conserved orthologs throughout Eukaryota, including in Aspergillus and yeast.
source: CAPN7 has evolutionarily conserved orthologs throughout Eukaryota, including in Aspergillus and yeast, where its role in ESCRT-dependent pH signaling is well described (Denison et al., 1995; Orejas et al., 1995; Futai et al., 1999; Peñalva et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In Aspergillus, pH signaling requires proteolytic activation of the transcription factor PacC.
source: In Aspergillus, pH signaling requires proteolytic activation of the transcription factor PacC (no known human ortholog), which initiates an adaptive transcriptional response.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge of Aspergillus pH signaling.

claim: PacC is cleaved and activated by the MIT domain-containing, Calpain-like CAPN7 ortholog protease PalB.
source: PacC is cleaved and activated by the MIT domain-containing, Calpain-like CAPN7 ortholog protease PalB, which is recruited to membrane-associated ESCRT-III filaments in response to alkaline pH through a MIT:MIM interaction with the ESCRT-III protein Vps24 (CHMP3 ortholog) (Rodríguez-Galán et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: PalB is recruited to membrane-associated ESCRT-III filaments in response to alkaline pH through a MIT:MIM interaction with the ESCRT-III protein Vps24.
source: PacC is cleaved and activated by the MIT domain-containing, Calpain-like CAPN7 ortholog protease PalB, which is recruited to membrane-associated ESCRT-III filaments in response to alkaline pH through a MIT:MIM interaction with the ESCRT-III protein Vps24 (CHMP3 ortholog) (Rodríguez-Galán et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: ESCRT assemblies in Aspergillus pH signaling contain PalA (ALIX ortholog), which co-recruits PacC to serve as a PalB substrate.
source: These ESCRT assemblies also contain PalA (ALIX ortholog), which co-recruits PacC to serve as a PalB substrate (Xu and Mitchell, 2001; Vincent et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The pH signaling system in fungi has striking parallels with the model for human CAPN7 functions in cytokinesis.
source: The pH signaling system in fungi has striking parallels with our model for human CAPN7 functions in cytokinesis, including: (1) MIT:MIM interactions between CAPN7 and ESCRT-III, which serve to recruit the protease to a key ESCRT signaling site. (2) The local presence of the homologous PalA and ALIX proteins. In the pH sensing system, PalA is thought to act as a scaffold that 'presents' the substrate to PalB for proteolysis on ESCRT-III assemblies, thus providing an extra level of spatiotemporal specificity for proteolysis. In the mammalian midbody, ALIX helps to nucleate ESCRT-III filament formation. (3) A requirement for proteolysis in downstream signal transduction.
evidence: This claim is a comparative analysis drawing parallels between fungal and human systems.

claim: ESCRT-III assemblies are evolutionarily conserved platforms that recruit and unite active calpain proteases and their substrates with spatiotemporal specificity to regulate key biological processes.
source: Thus, ESCRT-III assemblies are evolutionarily conserved platforms that recruit and unite active calpain proteases and their substrates with spatiotemporal specificity to regulate key biological processes.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from comparison of fungal and human ESCRT-calpain systems.
